Ice covers much of the Arctic Ocean in the winter, and some of it remains year-round. As EPA’s Arctic Sea Ice indicator explains, this ice plays vital roles in supporting healthy Arctic ecosystems and sustaining Indigenous Arctic Peoples’ traditional ways of life. It also influences broader climate patterns as its reflective surface and insulating effect help to moderate regional warming. As human activities warm the planet, the Arctic is warming more quickly than almost anywhere else on Earth, and sea ice is freezing later, melting sooner, and becoming thinner and less widespread.
